title: Binary puzzle with a unique solution
description: Generate a binary puzzle (Binairo, Takuzu): fill an n x n grid with 0s and 1s, with no three equal digits next to each other in a row or a column, as many 0s as 1s in every row and column, and no two equal rows or columns. The abstraction guesses a solved grid and the k cells to reveal; the check looks for two different grids that agree with all clues, and the refinement asks for a clue that contradicts one of them (as in sudoku-unique). The run stops at the first puzzle.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The size of the grid and the domains. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% A binary puzzle (Binairo, Takuzu) on an n x n grid, n even: fill every cell with 0 or 1.
% An instance may print clues pre(R,C,D).
#const n = 6.
row(1..n). col(1..n). dig(0;1).
printed(R,C) :- pre(R,C,_).

fragments.name: rules
fragments.description: The rules of the puzzle for any grid; used by solver A (one grid) and solver C (two grids).
fragments.text:
% The rules for every grid G that a solver declares with grid(G):
% cell(G,R,C,D) says that grid G has the digit D in row R, column C.
1 { cell(G,R,C,D) : dig(D) } 1 :- grid(G), row(R), col(C).
% No three equal digits next to each other in a row or a column.
:- cell(G,R,C,D), cell(G,R,C+1,D), cell(G,R,C+2,D).
:- cell(G,R,C,D), cell(G,R+1,C,D), cell(G,R+2,C,D).
% As many 0s as 1s in every row and every column.
:- grid(G), row(R), #count { C : cell(G,R,C,1) } != n/2.
:- grid(G), col(C), #count { R : cell(G,R,C,1) } != n/2.
% No two rows are equal, and no two columns.
:- grid(G), row(R1), row(R2), R1 < R2, #count { C : cell(G,R1,C,D), cell(G,R2,C,D) } = n.
:- grid(G), col(C1), col(C2), C1 < C2, #count { R : cell(G,R,C1,D), cell(G,R,C2,D) } = n.
% Every grid respects the printed clues.
:- grid(G), pre(R,C,D), not cell(G,R,C,D).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a solved grid and k of its cells as clues.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a solved grid s and k of its cells that are revealed as clues.
grid(s).
k { clue(R,C) : row(R), col(C), not printed(R,C) } k.
% given(R,C,D): the puzzle shows the digit D in row R, column C.
given(R,C,D) :- clue(R,C), cell(s,R,C,D).
#show given/3.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the clues with their digits. The solved grid stays private to solver A.
fragments.text: glue(given(R,C,D)) :- row(R), col(C), dig(D), not printed(R,C).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for two different grids that agree with all clues (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: two different grids a and b that both agree with the clues.
grid(a). grid(b).
:- given(R,C,D), not cell(a,R,C,D).
:- given(R,C,D), not cell(b,R,C,D).
differ :- cell(a,R,C,D), not cell(b,R,C,D).
:- not differ.
#show.
#show a(R,C,D) : cell(a,R,C,D).
#show b(R,C,D) : cell(b,R,C,D).

% Both grids fit every puzzle that shows only digits on which they agree. So a clue has
% to appear that contradicts one of them: any digit in a cell where a or b has the other.
both(R,C,D) :- cell(a,R,C,D), cell(b,R,C,D).
relevant(given(R,C,D)) :- row(R), col(C), dig(D), not printed(R,C), not both(R,C,D).

fragments.name: view
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.
fragments.text:
% The grid; printed clues shaded.
#program scene.
draw(layout(grid)).
draw(cell(R,C)) :- row(R), col(C).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, D)) :- pre(R,C,D).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, printed)) :- pre(R,C,_).

#program frame.
% The candidate's clues.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, V)) :- cand(given(R,C,V)).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, clue)) :- cand(given(R,C,_)).
% A counterexample: two solutions a and b; the cells where they differ show (a, b).
differs(R,C,(V,W)) :- cex(a(R,C,V)), cex(b(R,C,W)), V != W.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, differ)) :- differs(R,C,_).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, L)) :- differs(R,C,L).
draw(note("Two solutions fit the clues; they differ in the coloured cells (a, b).")) :- kind(reject).
draw(note("One solution: the puzzle is done.")) :- kind(solution).
#show draw/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts: % No printed clues: a 6 x 6 puzzle with k = 6 clues.
% All 4 x 4 puzzles with 4 clues and one solution (72 grids; checked by brute force).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The blocking loop: every refuted candidate is blocked on its own.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to 3 counterexamples per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + rules + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

generators.name: printed
generators.description: A random solved 6 x 6 grid (one of three grids, transposed, mirrored and with 0 and 1 swapped at random), each cell printed with probability p/1000. Set the instance constant n = 6.
generators.text:
% printed: one of three solved 6 x 6 grids (row R as a binary number), transposed, mirrored and flipped at random; each cell printed with probability p/1000
base(1,1,50). base(1,2,44). base(1,3,19). base(1,4,38). base(1,5,13). base(1,6,25).
base(2,1,42). base(2,2,22). base(2,3,37). base(2,4,11). base(2,5,52). base(2,6,25).
base(3,1,19). base(3,2,52). base(3,3,42). base(3,4,21). base(3,5,44). base(3,6,11).
bd(I,R,C,(V/(2**(6-C)))\2) :- base(I,R,V), C = 1..6.
g0(R,C,D) :- bd(I,R,C,D), I = @int(1, 3, base).
g1(R,C,D) :- g0(R,C,D), @int(0, 1, transpose) = 0.
g1(C,R,D) :- g0(R,C,D), @int(0, 1, transpose) = 1.
g2(R+M*(7-2*R),C,D) :- g1(R,C,D), M = @int(0, 1, mirrorrows).
g3(R,C+M*(7-2*C),D) :- g2(R,C,D), M = @int(0, 1, mirrorcols).
g(R,C,(D+@int(0, 1, swap))\2) :- g3(R,C,D).
pre(R,C,D) :- g(R,C,D), @flip(p, R, C, show) = 1.
#show pre/3.
